title: The Tripod Grip
summary: Hold the pencil about an inch above the tip, resting it between your thumb and index finger with your middle finger supporting it underneath.

steps.instruction: Hold the pencil about an inch above the tip, resting it lightly between your thumb and index finger with your middle finger supporting it underneath. This "tripod grip" keeps your knuckles from blocking your view of what you're writing.

title: Angle Your Paper
summary: Tilt your paper clockwise, with the top-right corner pointing roughly toward the middle of your body.

steps.instruction: Tilt your paper clockwise by up to 45 degrees, with the top-right corner pointing roughly toward the middle of your body. This lets your hand slide smoothly under the writing line instead of curling over it.

title: Keep Your Wrist Straight
summary: Keep your wrist straight instead of curling it over your writing — a hooked wrist causes more strain and messier handwriting over time.

steps.instruction: Keep your wrist straight instead of curling it over your writing — a hooked wrist causes more strain and messier handwriting over time.

title: Grips & Wide Barrels
summary: Triangular or extra-wide pencils naturally encourage the tripod grip, and a moulded finger grip works just as well on a pencil you already like.

steps.instruction: Pencils and pens with a triangular or extra-wide barrel naturally encourage the tripod grip and are easier for small hands to control. A moulded finger grip that slides onto a normal pencil works just as well if you already have one you like.

title: Whiteboard Smudge Fix
summary: If you're writing on a whiteboard or chalkboard, try holding your hand slightly higher than the line you're writing to avoid smudging as you go.

steps.instruction: If you're writing on a whiteboard or chalkboard, try holding your hand slightly higher than the line you're writing to avoid smudging as you go.

title: Spiral Notebook Flip
summary: When using a spiral notebook, flip it so the spiral is on the right, or look for notebooks made with left-handed layouts.

steps.instruction: When using a spiral notebook, flip it so the spiral is on the right, or look for notebooks made with left-handed layouts.

title: Offset-Tip Pens
summary: Pens with the tip angled off from the barrel keep your fingers back from wet ink and give a clearer view of the line.

steps.instruction: Some pens are made with the tip angled slightly off from the barrel, which keeps your fingers back from the wet ink and gives a clearer view of the line as you write. They take a little getting used to, but many left-handers find them worth trying.

title: Practice a Lighter Grip
summary: Try writing on paper stacked over carbon paper — the goal is to write clearly without leaving a mark on the sheets underneath.

steps.instruction: If you tend to press hard, try writing on a few sheets of paper stacked with carbon paper between them. The goal is to write clearly on the top sheet without leaving a mark on the ones underneath — a simple way to train a lighter, more relaxed hold.

title: Real Left-Handed Scissors
summary: The blades are reversed, not just the handles — and true left- and right-handed scissors can't both be one "universal" pair.

steps.instruction: Real left-handed scissors have the blades reversed, not just the handles — the top blade sits on the left so you can actually see your cutting line. Watch out for scissors marketed as "universal" or "ambidextrous": true left- and right-handed scissors can't both be one pair, since the blades themselves would need to face opposite ways.

title: Which Way the Waste Falls
summary: When cutting, always cut so the waste piece falls to the right of the blade — it keeps your view of the line clear.

steps.instruction: When cutting, always cut so the waste piece falls to the right of the blade — it keeps your view of the line clear.

title: Flip Right-Handed Scissors
summary: If you only have right-handed scissors, flipping them upside down changes the blade orientation, even if the finger holes feel a little off.

steps.instruction: If you only have right-handed scissors, flipping them upside down changes the blade orientation, even if the finger holes feel a little off.

title: Cut Counter-Clockwise
summary: Cut around shapes in an anti-clockwise direction — it keeps the piece you're cutting visible instead of hidden under the blades.

steps.instruction: Cut around shapes in an anti-clockwise direction — it keeps the piece you're cutting visible instead of hidden under the blades.

title: Craft Knife Safety
summary: A retractable craft knife is pushed out with your thumb either way — a secure, non-slip grip matters more than which hand you use.

steps.instruction: Craft knives with a retractable blade are pushed out using your thumb, so a left-handed grip should feel just as secure as a right-handed one — the key is a comfortable, non-slip grip rather than a knife "made for" either hand. Always use these with an adult around.

title: Left-Handed Desks
summary: A proper left-handed desk has the writing surface attached on the left side, not just a flat desk — worth requesting at school if you're stuck with a right-handed one.

steps.instruction: A proper left-handed desk has the writing surface attached on the left side, not just a flat desk — worth requesting at school if you're stuck with a right-handed one.

title: Computer Mice
summary: If the buttons feel backwards, your computer's settings let you swap the primary and secondary click in a couple of taps.

steps.instruction: Standard mice work fine for most left-handers as-is, but if the buttons feel backwards, your computer's settings (usually under "Mouse" in system settings) let you swap the primary and secondary click to the other button in a couple of taps.

title: Winding Clocks & Toys
summary: Wind-up toys and clocks are designed to be wound clockwise (a right-handed motion) — winding them the "wrong" way can actually damage the mechanism, so it takes some getting used to.

steps.instruction: Wind-up toys and clocks are designed to be wound clockwise (a right-handed motion) — winding them the "wrong" way can actually damage the mechanism, so it takes some getting used to.

title: Ring Binder Placement
summary: Ring binders and notebooks with rings on the left edge dig into your writing hand — look for ones with the rings at the top instead.

steps.instruction: Ring binders and notebooks with rings on the left edge dig into your writing hand — look for ones with the rings at the top instead.

title: Power Tool Safety
summary: Power tools often have safety switches and guards positioned for right-handed use, so extra care and a steady grip matter more if you ever use them.

steps.instruction: Power tools often have safety switches and guards positioned for right-handed use, so extra care and a steady grip matter more if you ever use them.

title: Sitting Next to Others
summary: When sitting at a shared table or desk, sitting to the left of a right-handed person avoids constant elbow bumping for both of you.

steps.instruction: When sitting at a shared table or desk, sitting to the left of a right-handed person avoids constant elbow bumping for both of you.

title: Learning by Mirroring
summary: Ask someone right-handed to sit facing you rather than beside you — their motions will naturally mirror what your left hand needs to do.

steps.instruction: When someone right-handed is showing you how to do something new, ask them to sit facing you instead of next to you. Their hand motions will then appear as a mirror image of what your left hand needs to do, which is often much easier to copy than trying to translate "left" and "right" from an explanation.

title: Tying Shoelaces
summary: A simple 6-step method for tying a bow, left-handed.

steps.instruction: Cross the left lace over the right, tuck it underneath, and pull both ends snug to make the base knot.
Fold the lace in your left hand into a loop and pinch the base of it between your finger and thumb.
Wrap the other lace around that loop.
Push the wrapped lace underneath itself to form a second loop.
Hold the new loop in one hand and the first loop in the other.
Pull both loops apart evenly to tighten the bow.

title: Reading Rulers
summary: Rulers with numbers starting from the left edge only can be awkward to read left-handed — look for ones printed both directions.

steps.instruction: Rulers with numbers starting from the left edge only can be awkward to read left-handed — look for ones printed both directions.

title: Handed Kitchen Gadgets
summary: Can openers, pencil sharpeners, and vegetable peelers are also worth checking — a lot of "gadget" tools are handed even when they don't look like it.

steps.instruction: Can openers, pencil sharpeners, and vegetable peelers are also worth checking — a lot of "gadget" tools are handed even when they don't look like it.

title: Wearing Watches
summary: Watches and other wrist accessories are usually made assuming a right-handed wearer — nothing wrong with wearing yours flipped if it's more comfortable.

steps.instruction: Watches and other wrist accessories are usually made assuming a right-handed wearer — nothing wrong with wearing yours flipped if it's more comfortable.

title: Left-Handed Keyboards
summary: A detachable number pad you place on your left is a cheaper fix than swapping a whole keyboard.

steps.instruction: The number pad on most keyboards sits to the right, which can mean extra reaching and strain for a left-handed typist doing a lot of data entry. A detachable, separate number pad you can place on your left is a cheaper fix than swapping the whole keyboard.

title: The Lefty Advantage
summary: In sports like tennis, fencing, and boxing, being left-handed can actually be an advantage since opponents are less used to your angle and timing.

steps.instruction: In sports like tennis, fencing, and boxing, being left-handed can actually be an advantage since opponents are less used to your angle and timing.

title: Tell Your Coach Early
summary: Let your coach or instructor know you're left-handed early on, especially for sports like golf, cricket, or gymnastics where the standard teaching is right-handed.

steps.instruction: Let your coach or instructor know you're left-handed early on, especially for sports like golf, cricket, or gymnastics where the standard teaching is right-handed.

title: Left-Handed Gear
summary: Left-handed baseball gloves and cricket gear exist — using the correct gear instead of adapting right-handed gear makes a real difference.

steps.instruction: Left-handed baseball gloves and cricket gear exist — using the correct gear instead of adapting right-handed gear makes a real difference.

title: Room in Group Lessons
summary: In group sports lessons, try to stand or sit so your dominant side has room to move without bumping a right-handed teammate's elbow.

steps.instruction: In group sports lessons, try to stand or sit so your dominant side has room to move without bumping a right-handed teammate's elbow.

title: Guitar Options
summary: Most guitars are strung for right-handed players — you can learn the standard way, restring one for left-handed play, or flip a right-handed guitar upside down like Jimi Hendrix did.

steps.instruction: Most guitars are strung for right-handed players — you can learn the standard way, restring one for left-handed play, or flip a right-handed guitar upside down like Jimi Hendrix did.

title: Not All Instruments Need Adapting
summary: Not all instruments need adapting — instruments played with both hands equally, like the clarinet, don't require a "left-handed version."

steps.instruction: Not all instruments need adapting — instruments played with both hands equally, like the clarinet, don't require a "left-handed version."

title: Restrung Guitar, Long Term
summary: If you're serious about guitar, a properly restrung left-handed model will feel more natural long-term than constantly adapting to a right-handed one.

steps.instruction: If you're serious about guitar, a properly restrung left-handed model will feel more natural long-term than constantly adapting to a right-handed one.

title: Piano, Drums & Hand Independence
summary: For piano, drums, and most orchestral instruments, hand dominance matters much less since both hands are trained separately from the start.

steps.instruction: For piano, drums, and most orchestral instruments, hand dominance matters much less since both hands are trained separately from the start.

title: Left-Handed Can Openers
summary: A left-handed opener lets your stronger left hand do the turning while your right hand steadies the can, safer near the sharp edge.

steps.instruction: A right-handed can opener forces you to either reach awkwardly across your body or turn the handle with your weaker hand. A left-handed opener flips this around, so your stronger left hand does the turning while your right hand steadies the can — much safer near a sharp edge.

title: Vegetable Peelers
summary: The safest motion is pulling the peeler toward you while your thumb braces the fruit — a right-handed peeler in your left hand faces the wrong way for this.

steps.instruction: The safest peeling motion is to pull the peeler toward you, bracing the fruit or vegetable with your thumb. A right-handed peeler held in your left hand has the blade facing the wrong way for this, so peeling ends up pushed away from the body instead, which gives much less control. A left-handed or double-edged peeler fixes this.

title: Bread Knives
summary: Standard serrations straighten a right-hander's twist as they saw — in a left hand they exaggerate it instead, curving the slice.

steps.instruction: Most bread knives are serrated on the side that straightens out a right-hander's natural inward twist as they saw. Held in a left hand, those same serrations exaggerate the twist instead, curving the slice — a symmetrical or reverse-serrated bread knife saws straight for a lefty.

title: Opening Jars, Taps & Lids
summary: Turning counter-clockwise is a naturally stronger motion for a left hand — that's why jars often feel easier to open than to close.

steps.instruction: Turning something counter-clockwise is a naturally stronger, more controlled motion for a left hand than turning clockwise. That's why jars, bottle tops, and taps often feel easier to open than to close — it's not just in your head.

title: Wooden Spoons & Spatulas
summary: Straight wooden spoons and most spatulas are naturally ambidextrous, so you don't need a special version of everything in the kitchen.

steps.instruction: Straight wooden spoons and most spatulas are naturally ambidextrous, so you don't need a special version of everything in the kitchen.

title: Measuring Cups & Jugs
summary: Measuring cups and jugs with the markings only on one side can be hard to read left-handed — look for ones with markings on both sides.

steps.instruction: Measuring cups and jugs with the markings only on one side can be hard to read left-handed — look for ones with markings on both sides.
